title: BUG: real Harbour app heavy-install wedges at modulesLoaded:0 on live OS (blocks live-app-render witness)
description:
## Problem

During HAR-694 real-substrate verification (2026-06-20), installing + opening the **real "Harbour" App Store app** on `os.harbour.cat` **wedges at** `modulesLoaded:0` (~226s observed) — the app never finishes startup, so it never renders in the iframe. This matches the prior "preview never bound iframeSrc" failure shape.

This is an **app startup / install hang — NOT a SW/transport defect.** HAR-694 proved on the live substrate that brokered first-open transport serves **200 cold + warm** and self-heals after a forced SW-table clear. The render still fails because the app process never reaches a loaded state.

## Why it matters

This is one of **two non-transport confounds** keeping HAR-694's `os-test-e2e-network` (`live-app-render`) gate **RED**:

1. **(this ticket)** Harbour heavy-install wedge at `modulesLoaded:0`.
2. LinearViewer `server.js:150` top-level `await dbClient.connect()` before `app.listen()` — tracked on **HAR-693**.

As written, HAR-694's gate "can never go green" while either confound stands. Splitting this out (per the HAR-694 review, comment `893b1fe2`) lets HAR-694 prove transport via a transport-pure witness while the real-app render confounds are fixed on their own tickets.

## Evidence

* HAR-694 PR #608 (`har-694-red-gate`, head `c5e78c9`) substrate runs; recap: *"Harbour install wedged at modulesLoaded:0 (226s)"*.
* Two independent HAR-694 sessions (implementation pivot + review) converge on this as a distinct startup/install bug.

## Acceptance (real substrate)

A real App Store install->open of the **Harbour** app on the live OS reaches `modulesLoaded > 0` and renders **styled** in the iframe; capture a render screenshot + supporting console/telemetry. CI/synthetic green is not sufficient.

comments.body:
## HAR-697 investigation — root cause (codebase + history analysis)

**TL;DR:** The `modulesLoaded:0` wedge is not a Harbour-app quirk — it is the **install-side manifestation of a substrate-class fault**: the harbour runtime funnels *all* synchronous filesystem I/O for *every* Worker through a **single OPFS helper Worker** (one event loop), and callers block in `Atomics.wait` with **no timeout, no fairness, and no stall-recovery**. A heavy npm install drives an enormous volume of serialized fs round-trips through that one chokepoint; the app's module loader then cannot make progress, so `modulesLoaded` never leaves 0.

### Re-grounding / staleness check (ticket created 2026-06-20)
Two commits touched the runtime since the ticket: **HAR-694** (`650e274`) and **HAR-701** (`8059800`). I re-read the boot-read path at HEAD. **Neither fixes this wedge.** HAR-701's commit message claims it "also benefits HAR-697", but its fix is `makeStatObject` Date timestamps fixing an `express.static`→`send` crash — a **serve-time** failure that can only occur *after* `modulesLoaded > 0` and the server is listening. It cannot touch a hang that happens *before the first module loads*. **The ticket remains valid; the wedge stands.** (It is correctly distinct from HAR-693's app-side mongo TLA confound.)

### Evidence (file:line)
1. **Single serialized fs chokepoint.** Every Worker's sync fs (`readFileSync`/`writeFileSync`/`stat`/`readdir`/…) round-trips through one adapter-singleton helper Worker via SharedArrayBuffer + `Atomics.wait` — `opfs-helper-entry.js:1-48`, `:135` (`endpoints` Map), `:715-735` (`dispatchKick`→`handleKick`, single loop, serial, **no prioritization**), `:899-909` (`withPathLock` — cross-endpoint FIFO mutex keyed by absolute path).
2. **Unbounded blocking wait.** Caller-side `waitForResponse` defaults to `timeoutMs = Infinity` → `Atomics.wait(…, undefined)` blocks forever — `opfs-sync-bridge.js:892-899`. The boot read path (`readFileSyncBlocking` `:1235-1263`) uses this default. If the helper never answers, the module loader's first `require()` parks permanently.
3. **Install amplifies fs through the same helper.** App install is `node install-<id>.mjs && <runCommand>` (`app-installer.js:745`); the installer runs `npm install` (`:399`). Tarball extraction writes **every dependency file + mkdirs every parent** through tier4 fs → the helper bridge — documented verbatim at `npm/tarball.js:8` (`fs.writeFileSync via tier4 fs → OPFS via the helper bridge`), loop at `:185-198`/`:228-238`. A "heavy" tree = thousands of serialized SAB round-trips on one event loop.
4. **`modulesLoaded:0` = first module read never returned.** `recordResolution()` increments `moduleLoadCount` once per resolved module (`module-loader.js:273`), then posts the boot-progress `moduleCount` frame (`:319-323`); the adapter re-emits it (`spawn.js:961`) and `boot-event-handlers.js:391-407` persists it onto the process record. Stuck at exactly 0 ⇒ the very first read never came back.
5. **No recovery for a stall, and the crash path has a gap.** `failInflightKicks` (`spawn.js:1443-1447`) only writes EAGAIN into endpoints **live/inflight at crash time** — a kick that *arrives after* the helper has died (or a helper that **stalls without crashing**, e.g. OPFS sync-handle exhaustion / `NoModificationAllowedError` contention under a heavy write load) is never released. The only boot watchdog (`boot-event-handlers.js:145-182`, `SLOW_BOOT_WATCHDOG_MS = 10000`) is **debug-gated** (arms only on HARBOUR_DEBUG heartbeats) and merely **logs** — it never kills or unblocks. So on a normal live boot nothing fires; the process just sits at `modulesLoaded:0`. The ~226s observation is "how long the harness waited," not a timeout.

### Is it isolated or a class? → **CLASS issue**
This substrate underlies **every** harbour Worker's startup: every App Store/URL/CLI/git/npm/upload install, every brokered `spawnSync` server (HAR-694), and direct workers all serialize fs through the one helper with the same unbounded wait. Any sufficiently heavy install — or any fs-heavy boot concurrent with one — can wedge identically. The proximate trigger varies (saturation vs. handle-lock stall vs. post-crash stranded kick); the **single unbounded, unmonitored, serial fs chokepoint** is the shared root. HAR-697 is the Harbour-app witness of it.

### Recommended next action (implementation task)
The evidence supports a real substrate fix, not more investigation:
1. **Bound the boot-critical wait** — give module-loader's reads (or `waitForResponse` on the boot path) a finite timeout so a stalled helper surfaces as an error instead of an infinite hang.
2. **Helper liveness / stall detection** — cover the post-crash-kick and stall-without-crash gaps `failInflightKicks` misses (heartbeat or re-check helper alive around a kick).
3. **Reduce install→boot fs amplification / add fairness** — pipeline-batch install writes and/or prioritize boot reads over bulk install writes on the helper loop.
4. **Make the wedge observable live** — un-gate (or `process_diag`-poll) the slow-boot watchdog during a real heavy-install repro to capture *which* `lastSpecifier` the first read stalls on — this directly answers the ticket's open question ("has the live substrate been re-tested / does any telemetry pinpoint the wedge").

**Scope note:** This is a codebase + git-history root-cause analysis. I did **not** run the live-substrate repro — that (capturing `modulesLoaded > 0` + a styled render screenshot of the real Harbour app) remains the acceptance gate for the eventual fix, per the ticket. Leaving status **In Progress** and the `Bug` label in place; this is ready to hand to an implementation task.

## HAR-705 diagnostic feed → HAR-697 (live `modulesLoaded:0` capture)

Live `@jkershaw/harbour` Featured-install → open on a fresh build (HAR-702 watchdog un-gated + boot read bounded). Full detail on HAR-705 / PR #617 / `harbour-os/docs/har-697-live-install-wedge.md`.

**Stalling specifier + timing:** `lastSpecifier = null` throughout; `modulesLoaded` stuck at **0** at 7s / 13s / 56s. No `boot-progress` frame ever emitted, so the slow-boot watchdog **never armed**, and the bounded boot read **never produced `ETIMEDOUT`**.

**Why the watchdog/bounded-read saw nothing:** they instrument the app's module-load **read** path. This wedge is **upstream** — the nested npm-install child exits 0 while persisting **nothing** to OPFS (`apps/npm-jkershaw-harbour/` has only `package.json`), so the launch dies on `./node_modules/.bin/harbour: not found` and the app program never loads a module.

**Proximate trigger (classification):** **nested-child silent zero-write install** — HAR-697's shared-OPFS-helper durability/fairness family, but manifesting as a lost-write, not a blocking `Atomics.wait`. A top-level `npm install` succeeds (3 pkgs, 20s); re-launch with `node_modules` present boots to `listening` in ~6s and **renders the full styled UI** — so there is **no second, module-load-time wedge** in this app on this build.

**Implications for the fix:**
1. On the current build the live `modulesLoaded:0` is **dominated by an install-phase silent no-op**, upstream of any module-load fs stall.
2. The fairness/durability fix must cover the **nested-child write path** (npm spawned inside the app process), not just the app's module-load read path.
3. HAR-702's watchdog/bounded-read will **not** catch this class — it needs install-phase observability (shipped diagnostically in PR #617: fail-loud when install exits 0 but `node_modules/<pkg>` is missing).

### HAR-705 addendum — two extra signals from CI

1. **An in-installer post-install `existsSync` guard is unsound.** Tried a fail-loud "install exited 0 but `node_modules/<pkg>` missing" check inside the installer; CI's `@network` lane (green on main) false-fired it for both `@jkershaw/harbour` and `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`. The installer process cannot see files its own `npm` child wrote through the OPFS helper — per-Worker fs-shadow staleness (the same cross-thread visibility rule in CLAUDE.md). Implication: the durability fix must invalidate/refresh that shadow (or the guard must run from a fresh process). Guard reverted.

2. **The `@phase-e-gate` live-render gate is nondeterministically red on the wedge.** On a docs-only commit (code identical to main) the non-blocking `os-test-e2e-network` lane failed exactly one test — `Featured install → open → RENDERS STYLED · Harbour @phase-e-gate`: *"Harbour preview window never bound a /__hr/ iframeSrc."* That is this bug firing in CI, not just on the live OS. The lane is `continue-on-error: true`, so it doesn't gate merges, but it's a reproducible CI witness for the wedge.

why: REAL full-scale HAR-697 frozen after HAR-705 refuted the module-load-stall cause and before the review filed HAR-707. The refutation is buried after a multi-thousand-char investigation that ends "ready to hand to an implementation task", so the trail is dense with fix-oriented prose around a refuted, unvalidated cause whose decisive live experiment never passed. Correct: re-investigate / run the decisive experiment; advancing to implement is the fix-before-validate trap. Real-scale counterpart to the forgiving synthetic SYN-21.
